kpis.project_name: SANTANDER CONSUMER USA INC. - Technology Operations and Delivery Support Resources SOW 2023

risks.title: Resource Availability and Performance Issues
risks.reason: Historical pattern shows 2 out of 3 risks (67%) in SANTANDER project were related to resource challenges including unavailability, skill gaps, and performance issues. Resource unavailability was mitigated but assessed as Moderate severity with Likely occurrence.
recommendedActions: Establish backup resource pool with cross-trained team members
Create knowledge transfer documentation for critical roles
risks.preventiveActions: Maintain a shadow resource for each critical role; conduct quarterly skill assessments and provide targeted training on Data Quality lifecycle, SQL profiling, and data warehouse concepts
risks.mitigation: Engage Offshore/Onshore Leads to split time 75% development & 25% mentoring; involve Ascendion Data Engineering practice team in assessment and upskilling
risks.contingency: Have ELT (Experienced Lead Technical) resources in place who can shadow current team and take over responsibilities immediately if primary resources become unavailable
relatedHistoricalRisks: Resources & Skill Gap - Offshore developers lacking confidence in Data Quality lifecycle

risks.title: SLA Commitment and Performance Measurement Challenges
risks.reason: SOW explicitly mentions SLA requirements with non-performance discounts applicable. Historical risk identified that complete traceability and measurement of SLA is challenging due to fit-shoring completion dependency and contractor presence at onshore. Risk assessed as Severe with Likely occurrence.
recommendedActions: Establish unit of measure for SLA for each track
Jointly review with client and publish results
risks.preventiveActions: For each track, mutually agree upon the unit of measure for the SLA before fit-shoring completion; establish baseline metrics and automated collection mechanisms
risks.mitigation: Collect the performance measurement metrics on a monthly basis and jointly review with Santander Consumer USA to ensure transparency and alignment on SLA achievement
risks.contingency: Document all SLA deviations with root cause analysis; negotiate penalty waivers for deviations caused by client-side dependencies or scope changes
relatedHistoricalRisks: SLA commitment - Penalties applicable as per SOW will be levied on Ascendion

risks.title: Quality and Technical Skill Gap in Data Engineering
risks.owner: Technical Lead / Data Engineering Practice Lead
risks.reason: Historical evidence shows offshore developers not showing confidence with Data Quality lifecycle/process and lacking awareness of SQL Profiling & data warehouse concepts. This was assessed as Moderate severity with Likely occurrence and mitigated status.
recommendedActions: Conduct SQL and Data Warehousing upskilling programs
Implement peer code reviews and mentoring sessions
Establish Data Quality best practices documentation
Schedule regular technical workshops with Data Engineering practice team
risks.preventiveActions: Involve Ascendion Data Engineering practice team in initial assessment and ongoing training; create structured learning paths for SQL profiling and data warehouse concepts
risks.mitigation: Data Quality team Offshore/Onshore Leads to play an active role in mentoring and monitoring the work of team; allocate 25% of lead time for mentoring and supporting team members
risks.contingency: Bring in senior Data Engineering consultants from Ascendion practice team for critical deliverables; consider resource swaps if skill gaps cannot be closed within acceptable timeframe
relatedHistoricalRisks: Resources & Skill Gap - Offshore developers not aware of SQL Profiling & data warehouse concepts

likelihoodTrends.distribution: 67% Likely occurrence rate indicates high probability of risk materialization

impactTrends.description: 100% of risks have High or Very High impact, indicating significant business consequences if risks materialize

statusDistribution.description: All 3 risks remain active with mitigation strategies in place; 2 risks mitigated, 1 assessed

sequence: Quality issues in Data Quality lifecycle execution
SLA deviations and performance measurement challenges
Financial penalties and client relationship impact
risk_chains.description: Resource challenges including unavailability and skill gaps in SQL profiling and data warehouse concepts cascade into quality issues in Data Quality lifecycle execution, which then lead to SLA deviations. The SOW explicitly states that non-performance discounts will be applied to tracks with SLA deviation, creating financial and reputational risk.
risk_chains.mitigationApproach: Implement comprehensive resource management strategy with backup resources, structured mentoring programs (75% development / 25% mentoring split for leads), upskilling on SQL and Data Warehousing, and automated SLA tracking with monthly joint reviews with client

sequence: Offshore developers lacking confidence in Data Quality lifecycle
Inadequate SQL Profiling and data warehouse knowledge
risk_chains.description: Fundamental skill gaps in offshore team regarding Data Quality processes and technical capabilities create downstream quality and delivery risks that threaten client confidence and project success
risk_chains.mitigationApproach: Engage Ascendion Data Engineering practice team for assessment and training; implement structured mentoring with Offshore/Onshore Leads dedicating 25% time to team development; establish clear quality gates and peer review processes

strengths: Proactive risk identification with all 3 risks documented and tracked
Mitigation strategies defined for all identified risks
Client engagement established with plans for joint SLA reviews
Backup resources (ELT) identified and in shadowing mode
Escalation mechanisms in place with client management
weaknesses: 100% of risks are Organizational category indicating systemic resource and process challenges
67% of risks are resource-related showing dependency on people rather than process
All risks remain Active with no closures, indicating ongoing challenges
High likelihood (67% Likely) suggests risks are probable to materialize
SLA measurement framework not yet fully established despite contractual obligations
Skill gaps in critical technical areas (SQL, Data Warehousing, Data Quality lifecycle)
Heavy reliance on contractors at onshore impacting metrics collection
lessonsLearned: Resource availability must be validated continuously with backup plans in place before project start
SLA measurement framework and unit of measure must be agreed upon and baselined before fit-shoring completion
Technical skill assessment should be mandatory during resource onboarding with gap closure plans
Mentoring and knowledge transfer should be built into lead roles (25% allocation) from project inception
Automated metrics collection is essential for SLA tracking when contractors are involved
Data Engineering practice team involvement is critical for quality assurance in data-intensive projects
Client-side dependencies (like fit-shoring completion) should be tracked as external risks with contingency plans
successFactors: Structured mitigation plans with clear ownership (Offshore/Onshore Leads, Data Engineering practice team)
Client collaboration on SLA definition and joint monthly reviews
Backup resource strategy with ELT shadowing current team
Upskilling initiatives with practice team involvement
Regular monitoring and weekly reminders to team on performance expectations
Transparent communication with client on challenges and mitigation progress
